grammar_concept.title: Past Perfect: had + past participle
grammar_concept.rule: Use the Past Perfect (had + past participle) for an action that happened before another action or point in the past. It shows which of two past events happened first.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Quando há duas coisas no passado, o Past Perfect (had + particípio passado) marca qual delas aconteceu primeiro — a mais antiga das duas.
grammar_concept.example: When I arrived at the station, the train had already left. She had never been to Japan before that trip.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Quando cheguei à estação, o comboio já tinha partido. Ela nunca tinha estado no Japão antes dessa viagem.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Em português falado é comum usar o pretérito perfeito simples para as duas ações e deixar a ordem implícita pelo contexto ("Quando cheguei, o comboio partiu"). Em inglês, se a primeira ação aconteceu claramente antes da segunda, é necessário marcar isso com o Past Perfect: "When I arrived, the train had left" — só "the train left" fica ambíguo sobre qual aconteceu primeiro.
grammar_concept.correction: Duas ações no passado, uma claramente antes da outra → a mais antiga leva Past Perfect (had + particípio passado), a mais recente leva Past Simple. Sem essa marcação, a ordem das duas ações fica ambígua em inglês.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: A contar uma experiência: "By the time I got the job offer, I had already accepted another one."

vocabulary.definition_en: before now, or before a particular time in the past
example_sentences: The train had already left when I arrived.

vocabulary.definition_en: used to say that something had already happened before a particular moment
example_sentences: By the time I got home, everyone had left.
She had previously worked as a nurse.

exercises.prompt: Complete: When I arrived at the station, the train ___ (already/leave).
exercises.explanation: A ação do comboio partir aconteceu antes da chegada → Past Perfect.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar só o Past Simple ("already left") deixa ambígua a ordem das duas ações.

correct_answer: She had never been to Japan before that trip.
distractors: She never was to Japan before that trip.
She has never been to Japan before that trip.
She never had been to Japan before that trip.
exercises.explanation: "Had never been" é a ordem correta: had + never + particípio passado.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Colocar "never" antes de "had" é um erro comum de ordem das palavras.

exercises.explanation: "Previously" refere-se a um momento anterior ao que está a ser descrito.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What had happened by the time they got to the cinema?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "By the time we got to the cinema, the film had already started."
exercises.transcript: By the time we got to the cinema, the film had already started. We had to wait for the next showing.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "David felt nervous at the interview. He had prepared for weeks, but he had never done a job interview in English before." What had David never done before?
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente: "he had never done a job interview in English before".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Quando ela chegou, a reunião já tinha terminado."
correct_answer: When she arrived, the meeting had already finished.
When she arrived, the meeting had already ended.
exercises.explanation: "Já tinha terminado" corresponde ao Past Perfect ("had already finished"), não ao Past Simple.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar só o Past Simple ("the meeting already finished") em vez do Past Perfect é o erro mais comum aqui.

steps.content: In fast speech, "had" often reduces to 'd, especially after pronouns: "I had" → "I'd" /aɪd/, "she had" → "she'd" /ʃiːd/. This is the same contraction used for "would" — context tells you which one is meant.

steps.prompt: Tell a short story about a time you arrived somewhere and something had already happened before you got there.
Write 5 sentences about your life, using the Past Perfect to show which of two past events happened first.
